text:
morgan: quick question — I split our KMS policy out into a shared tf module and my `terraform plan` wants to replace the key (aws_kms_key.app) entirely. anyone run into this when moving policy ownership across modules?

sam: can you paste the plan snippet and the old vs new code? usually it's something in the key policy bytes that changed.

morgan: plan excerpt ->
```
~ resource "aws_kms_key" "app" {
    id = "1234abcd"
    # (changes to policy -> forces replacement)
}
+ resource "aws_kms_key" "app" {
    id = (known after apply)
}
```
I moved the policy from inline `policy = jsonencode(...)` in the key resource to an `aws_kms_key_policy` in module/keys. Terraform shows recreate.

lee: yep that's expected in some provider versions — key policy is sometimes treated as part of the resource identity. A couple of options:
- keep the policy inside the `aws_kms_key` resource (single source) while you split other iam grants out.
- OR manage the key policy in the separate resource but apply `lifecycle { create_before_destroy = true }` on the key so we don't get a delete-recreate window.

tiffany: another pattern: keep a very small stable key policy (root/admins) in the key resource and manage all app-specific permissions with `aws_kms_grant` + IAM role permissions (IRSA) — moving app principals into grants avoids changing the key resource often.

morgan: interesting. we're using IRSA roles for pods — the principal string format changed slightly when I switched to module output `role_arn` vs inline var, maybe that canonicalization triggers drift. any tips to make principal stable?

lee: canonicalize with `jsonencode` and avoid interpolated whitespace. also make sure the role principal uses the full ARN consistently: `arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/namespace-app-role` vs `arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/namespace-app-role ` (trailing space kills you).

sam: quick checklist when you see recreate:
- diff policy JSON exactly (copy both into a diff tool)
- check provider version change (some releases changed semantics)
- check if switching between `policy` attribute and `aws_kms_key_policy` resource is happening
- consider `create_before_destroy` + a canary environment apply

morgan: thanks. small follow-up: is `aws_kms_grant` sufficient for IRSA (EKS serviceaccount assuming role) or do we still need to touch key policy for the role to decrypt?

tiffany: grants are fine for encrypt/decrypt usage, but some KMS operations (like rekeying/management) are gated by the key policy. For runtime usage by pods, give the assumed role kms:Encrypt/kms:Decrypt via IAM and/or kms grants. Key policy should at minimum allow the account administrators to manage grants.

morgan: got it. last question: if I add `lifecycle { create_before_destroy = true }` to the key resource in the shared module, will that preserve the existing key ID for other resources?

lee: create_before_destroy will create the new key first, then destroy the old one, so resources that reference the exact key id may need update. It's safer to do a staged rollout: 1) create new key + grants, 2) update services to use new key (if you need to change id), 3) rotate/delete old. If you want zero-id-change, avoid recreating the key at all (try to update policy in-place).

morgan: ok i'll try the minimal-in-place approach first (keep key policy as-is in the key resource, move other stuff to grants). i'll run a canary in staging and report back. thanks all :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: tf apply staging-keys at 16:30 UTC (canary)

sam: ping if you want a quick pair on the staging apply, happy to watch the plan/apply with you.

morgan: appreciated — will DM when i'm ready.
